The initial stages are concerned with the collection and preparation of the raw material. First, used glass bottles are accumulated from designated recycling points and transported to a treatment facility. Upon arrival, they undergo a sorting process, where contaminants such as ceramics, metals, and coloured glass are removed to ensure the purity of the subsequent batch. The sorted glass is then thoroughly washed to eliminate any residual liquids, labels, or adhesives.

Following this cleansing phase, the prepared glass is fed into a crushing machine, which reduces it to small, uniform fragments known as cullet. This cullet is then transferred to a high-temperature furnace where it is melted into a viscous liquid. The molten glass is subsequently used in moulding machinery to form brand-new bottles, which are finally packaged and distributed to retailers and consumers, thus completing the perpetual loop.
